item.title: Chinese initiative gives fresh momentum to China-U.S. youth exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Out at sea, Chinese and U.S. university students explored the ocean, took part in scientific and cultural activities and, at one point, sat down to negotiate a global environmental problem. Taking on the roles of different countries and international organizations, 20 students, 10 from each country, worked on solutions to mercury pollution in the oceans. When one American student joked that they might have to leave the ship if they couldn't reach an agreement, the group erupted in laughter, recalled Zhou Xinyi, then a student representative from Tsinghua University. Zhou and her fellow students were participating in a program aboard the China-U.S. Youth Friendship vessel, which sailed from Hong Kong via Ningbo to Shanghai earlier this year. For them, the experience offered more than a journey across the sea -- it was an opportunity to learn, work together and build friendships. The voyage was one of many exchanges under an initiative China announced in November 2023 to invite 50,000 young Americans to China for exchange and study over five years, an effort to encourage them to learn about China as it really is and help build people-to-people ties. Since the initiative was launched, youth exchanges between the two countries have grown in both scale and variety. Many young Americans have come to China for exchanges and study, building friendships and helping strengthen ties across the Pacific. With efforts from various parties, the goal was reached two and a half years ahead of schedule earlier this year, with more than 50,000 young Americans from all 50 U.S. states and Washington, D.C., visiting China. They left footprints in all 31 provincial-level regions on the Chinese mainland, as well as Hong Kong and Macao, taking part in cultural experiences, language learning, academic programs, science and technology exchanges and sports activities, according to China's Ministry of Education. Meredith Kime, a PhD candidate in Earth and Environmental Sciences at Columbia University, who was also aboard the China-U.S. Youth Friendship vessel, said: "I wanted to come on this incredible journey, collaborating with students from the United States and China, enjoying friendship and our shared experience." Kime added that the initiative to invite 50,000 young Americans to China over five years has created a bridge for youths from the two countries to connect, giving real friendships a chance to grow. GROWING MOMENTUM Reaching the goal ahead of schedule reflects young Americans' strong desire to experience China firsthand and the powerful momentum for people-to-people exchanges, said Diao Daming, vice dean of the National Academy of Development and Strategy of Renmin University of China. The initiative is more than a numerical target. It has created a long-term, stable and sustainable platform for youth exchanges between the two countries, said David Chong, founder and president of the U.S.-China Youth and Student Exchange Association. Many young Americans who took part in exchange programs have continued to follow developments in China after returning home and some have taken up learning Chinese, while others have continued to promote exchanges between schools, he said. Wang Yijie, founder of Noice China, which organizes trips to China for U.S. students, has noticed the rising enthusiasm among U.S. students for visiting China. "Our team is really busy because we are hosting more groups this year," she said. "Spots for a recent trip involving about 160 Harvard students sold out in less than a minute." Wang said students who visit China often return home and encourage people around them to experience the country for themselves. The message they pass on to their friends and family is simple: "You have to go." The growing number of youth exchange programs shows that China's rapid development, particularly in emerging technologies, has drawn greater attention from young people, driving a rising interest in the country, she noted. More opportunities created by the initiative, along with more convenient travel policies, have made it easier for students to visit China. Many programs are now driven less by marketing than by recommendations within close-knit student networks, she said. LEGACY OF PEOPLE-TO-PEOPLE TIES History has shown that time and again, individuals on both sides have reached out to one another and helped put bilateral ties back on track during challenging periods. More than half a century ago, a small table tennis ball paved the way for the normalization of China-U.S. relations. This year marks the 55th anniversary of Ping-Pong Diplomacy, and a series of commemorative events have been held across the Pacific to carry on the spirit. Judy Hoarfrost, the youngest member of the U.S. table tennis delegation to China back in April 1971, returned to China to attend a commemoration ceremony in April this year and then led a U.S. pickleball delegation to China in May. "Fifty-five years ago, that trip to China changed my life," said Hoarfrost, who is 70. Now, seeing young people from the two countries playing and laughing side by side on the court, she said any relationship is built on friendship and trust. "I think it's really important to give youth those opportunities, because it's only by really meeting each other that you can understand what you have in common," Hoarfrost said. Beyond sports activities, cultural and technological exchanges have offered other ways for young people to connect. In January 2025, a video of the U.S. children's choir One Voice singing a popular Chinese song at Beijing's historic Temple of Heaven drew attention on social media. Since then, the choir has been invited to visit different regions of China, performing and interacting with local children. Some U.S. students have not only visited the Forbidden City and the Great Wall, but have also tried traditional Chinese medicine or learned calligraphy. After trying on a traditional Chinese costume, Tristan Rice from Western Carolina University said that no matter how vivid China may appear in streaming videos, nothing compares with seeing and experiencing it in person. For other students, visiting technology companies, such as Baidu's technology park and Xiaomi's automobile factory, offered a more complete picture of contemporary China. As China's tech sector, particularly the robotics industry, continues to thrive, global perceptions of the country's technological capabilities are changing profoundly. Back in 2008, Rebecca Fannin, author of "Silicon Dragon," predicted the rise of China's tech sector in her book, a forecast that was widely dismissed at the time. Today, the tide has turned. "We're looking to China as a leader of the futuristic vision -- that's a big change from the past," Fannin said during a program hosted by the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations, a non-profit dedicated to advancing bilateral understanding. U.S. student Ty DeVito was impressed by China's capacity for innovation during a visit to the Beijing Daxing International Hydrogen Energy Demonstration Zone. He hoped the two countries could build on their strengths and work together to advance green development. KEEPING EXCHANGES GOING Guided by the consensus reached by the two heads of state, there have been clear signs of stronger people-to-people exchanges and economic ties between China and the United States in recent months, experts say. An important framework for dialogue has been established, laying a solid strategic foundation for further narrowing differences, advancing practical cooperation and keeping China-U.S. relations on a steady course, said Wang Dong, executive director of the Institute for Global Cooperation and Understanding at Peking University. China's Ministry of Education has pledged to continue expanding the bilateral youth exchanges, turn short-term programs into long-term, stable cooperation, and encourage greater participation from non-governmental forces. These efforts are intended to give the initiative a lasting presence and bring greater vitality from young people to the steady, long-term development of China-U.S. relations, the ministry said. The initiative shows that China is committed to doing its part and further fostering dialogue between young people in both countries, David Firestein, president and CEO of the George H. W. Bush Foundation for U.S.-China Relations, said at a recent event. "I think the United States needs to do more, and I hope we'll see more," Firestein said. "Youth will shape our future," said Jan Berris, vice president of the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations. "It's really important for people to see for themselves what the other country is like, to have an opportunity to talk to others. Then you can make up your own mind," she said. ■

item.title: 48th WorldSkills Competition kicks off in Shanghai
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
The 48th WorldSkills Competition opens in east China's Shanghai, Sept. 22, 2026. Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the event, which was read out at the opening ceremony. Chinese Premier Li Qiang attended the opening ceremony and declared the competition open. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) SHANGHAI, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- The 48th WorldSkills Competition opened in Shanghai on Tuesday evening, with 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions vying in 64 skill events. Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the event, which was read out at the opening ceremony. Chinese Premier Li Qiang attended the opening ceremony and declared the competition open. China has sent 71 competitors, who will compete in all 64 events, covering six sectors -- transportation and logistics, construction and building technology, manufacturing and engineering technology, information and communication technology, creative arts and fashion, and social and personal services, according to organizers. The competition brings together young skilled professionals from around the world to showcase their expertise and exchange experience. The WorldSkills Conference 2026 and the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Expo will also be held alongside the competition. Competition events will conclude on Sept. 27. The WorldSkills Competition, held every two years and operated by WorldSkills International, is widely regarded as the world's leading vocational skills competition. Seven skills are making their debut at this year's competition, including rail vehicle technology, unmanned aerial systems, intelligent security technology and software testing, reflecting emerging industry trends and evolving demand for vocational skills. The changing mix of WorldSkills events has followed shifts in industries and occupations. The first competition, held in Spain in 1950, focused largely on traditional trades such as construction and manufacturing, while automation, the expansion of the service sector and the rise of the internet later brought new skills onto the competition floor. China joined WorldSkills International in 2010 and has since competed in seven editions of the competition. It has ranked first in both the gold-medal tally and overall group points at the past four editions. Official data showed that China has more than 220 million skilled workers, including over 72 million highly skilled workers. Skilled workers account for about 30 percent of the country's employed population, providing an important talent base for economic development and industrial upgrading. According to organizers, discussions at the WorldSkills Conference cover issues that include artificial intelligence, vocational education and future skills, bringing together policymakers, educators and industry representatives from around the world to exchange views on skills development and changing workforce needs. Skills development has also become an expanding area of cooperation between China and countries in the Global South. A total of 17 Luban Workshops, vocational education programs jointly set up by Chinese and overseas partner institutions, have been established in 15 African countries, training more than 10,000 young African people. At the Shanghai event, 10 African countries are jointly presenting an African exhibition area. ■ The Chinese national flag is carried during the opening ceremony of the 48th WorldSkills Competition in east China's Shanghai, Sept. 22, 2026. item.title: UN General Assembly begins general debate
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
The General Debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly is held at the UN headquarters in New York, Sept. 22, 2026. The General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly opened at the UN headquarters in New York on Tuesday. The theme of the general debate is "Restoring trust, managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all." (Xinhua/Zhang Fengguo) UNITED NATIONS, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- The General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly opened at the UN headquarters in New York on Tuesday. Khalilur Rahman, president of the 81st session of the General Assembly, presided over the opening of the debate, which is themed "Restoring trust, managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all." In his opening speech, Rahman stressed the importance of rebuilding trust. "Trust is not given. It is earned. And we earn trust, I believe, in three ways: first, by being unapologetically realistic about where we are falling behind; second, by taking a foundational look at the reforms of the UN to deliver better; and third, by making our work more inclusive and engaging all relevant stakeholders, from all parts of our society," he said. Rahman said UN member states have an opportunity in this session to show that they have learned from what works, that they are prepared to confront what does not, and that they can build a United Nations capable not simply of surviving change, but of shaping change. "To seize that opportunity, we must be realistic enough to confront hard truths, bold enough to reform, and inclusive enough to bring the right people to the table," he said. "That is how, in my view, we will renew trust in our organization and make it fit for future." In his "state-of-the-world" report right before the opening of this year's General Debate, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for a networked multipolar world, instead of one of fragmentation and transactionalism. "We are clearly moving towards a multipolar world. And that movement is irreversible. But there are different ways that multipolarity can take shape," Guterres said. "One possibility is a world of fragmentation and transactionalism. A world of rising tensions and deepening mistrust. Of fractured markets and weakened institutions. Of shrinking cooperation and zero-sum calculations. In many respects, that is the trajectory we are on today," he said. But there is another path -- a path toward networked multipolarity. A world built on interdependence, and sustained by a dense web of economic, political, social and technological connections; a world in which multiple centers of influence coexist within a common framework of international law and shared rules, said the UN chief. "Such a world can help us avoid hegemonic tendencies and also what I have called the Great Fracture: the division of the world into two rival blocs with separate economic, technological and security systems," he said. "A networked world recognizes that no power can solve today's challenges alone." A networked multipolar world can create the conditions for more balanced and representative global problem-solving, but it requires a multilateral system centered in the United Nations that is balanced and representative -- strong, effective institutions that reflect the realities and the progressively changing relative weight of countries and economies in today's world, not the power arrangements of 80 years ago, said Guterres. "Fortunately, we are not starting from scratch. We already have a binding foundation: the Charter of the United Nations. And the principles that give it life. The primacy of international law. Upholding human dignity. And the pursuit of justice in all its dimensions. These are the backbone for the effective, legitimate and responsible exercise of power in the 21st century," he said. ■ Khalilur Rahman (C), president of the 81st session of the General Assembly, speaks during the General Debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN headquarters in New York, Sept. 22, 2026. item.title: Beijing Culture Forum opens, focusing on cultural heritage, mutual learning among civilizations
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attends the 2026 Beijing Culture Forum and delivers a keynote speech in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 22, 2026. The 2026 Beijing Culture Forum opened in the Chinese capital on Tuesday. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei) BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 Beijing Culture Forum opened in the Chinese capital on Tuesday, bringing together more than 600 guests from 44 countries and regions to discuss cultural heritage protection and mutual learning among civilizations. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended the event and delivered a keynote speech. Participants from China and abroad said the China-proposed Global Civilization Initiative, together with efforts to promote international cooperation in cultural heritage and to build a community with a shared future for humanity, has been of great significance to advancing cultural heritage endeavors in China and around the world. They noted that cultural heritage is the shared asset of humanity and that preserving, passing down and making good use of cultural heritage is essential for the continuity of human civilization and sustainable global development. Participants urged strong commitment to safeguarding humanity's cultural heritage, adhering to the principles of protection first, rational utilization and minimum intervention in heritage conservation, and protecting cultural heritage as we protect our lives. They also called for closer exchanges of experience in cultural heritage protection, in areas such as cultural heritage surveys, legal frameworks, public participation and technological support, as well as expanded international cooperation in ancient civilization studies, joint archaeological projects, restoration of historical sites and museum exchanges. The participants said efforts should be made to improve global governance in cultural heritage protection, expand cooperation under multilateral mechanisms and promote cultural heritage protection in the Global South. The forum is jointly hosted by the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee and the Beijing Municipal Government. Beijing, with more than 3,000 years of history as a city and more than 870 years as a capital, is home to a wealth of World Heritage sites. The annual event comes as China continues to promote international cultural exchanges and cooperation through various platforms and initiatives. The Global Civilization Initiative, proposed by China in 2023, advocates respect for the diversity of civilizations, the common values of humanity, the importance of inheritance and innovation of civilizations, as well as robust international people-to-people exchanges and cooperation. ■ Guests attend the main forum of the 2026 Beijing Culture Forum in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 22, 2026. The 2026 Beijing Culture Forum opened here on Tuesday. Over 600 participants from 44 countries and regions attended the forum. item.title: Old Friends' Expectations
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
As Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares for his state visit to the United States on Sept. 23-25, his old American friends are sharing fond memories, and their expectations for the upcoming visit. "Xi Jinping is a friend who respects history, values people-to-people bonds, and keeps his word," one of Xi's old U.S. friends said. Produced by Xinhua Global Service ■

item.title: Xi's upcoming U.S. visit to chart course for bilateral ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
* Since Trump's return to the White House in 2025, the Chinese and U.S. heads of state have stayed in close contact, speaking by phone many times, exchanging letters on several occasions and meeting face to face twice since late last year. * Despite frictions and challenges, China-U.S. trade has demonstrated strong resilience. In the second quarter of this year, bilateral trade in goods grew 13.7 percent year on year. As of July this year, U.S. companies had established more than 84,000 enterprises in China. * In just over two and a half years, more than 50,000 young Americans from all 50 states have been invited to travel to different parts of China. They have toured smart factories, visited rural communities and experienced everyday life in places far from home. For many, the journeys have led to new friendships with Chinese peers. BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- At the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25, marking an exchange of visits between the two leaders within six months. As changes unseen in a century are accelerating and uncertainties continue to grow around the world, the visit is expected to bring greater stability and predictability to China-U.S. relations and beyond. CONSTRUCTIVE STRATEGIC STABILITY China-U.S. ties have been widely regarded as the world's most important bilateral relationship. More than 50 years ago, leaders from both countries, with remarkable courage and political vision, took the historic step of breaking the ice. Since then, the relationship has repeatedly found a way forward despite tensions and setbacks, with head-of-state diplomacy consistently providing strategic guidance. In recent years, China-U.S. relations have weathered ups and downs. How the world's two major countries manage their relationship matters far beyond their own borders. Hosting Trump in Beijing in May, Xi underscored the responsibilities shouldered by both countries in these changing times. "Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides Trap and create a new paradigm of major-country relations? Can we meet global challenges together and provide greater stability for the world? Can we build a bright future together for our bilateral relations in the interest of the well-being of the two peoples and the future of humanity? These are the questions vital to history, to the world and to the people," said Xi. Xi has repeatedly said that the broad Pacific Ocean is vast enough to embrace both China and the United States. He has also urged the two sides to be partners and friends, and work together to accomplish more great and concrete things for the good of the two countries and the whole world. Since Trump's return to the White House in 2025, the two leaders have stayed in close contact, speaking by phone many times, exchanging letters on several occasions and meeting face to face twice since late last year. "I look forward to working together with you to set the course and steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations, so as to make 2026 a historic, landmark year that opens up a new chapter in China-U.S. relations," Xi said in his meeting with Trump in May. It was during their Beijing meeting that the two leaders agreed on a new vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, providing strategic guidance for bilateral ties over the next three years and beyond. "The building of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability should not be a mere slogan, but concrete action taken by both sides toward the same goal," Xi said. He outlined the "constructive strategic stability" as a positive stability with cooperation as the mainstay, a sound stability with moderate competition, a constant stability with manageable differences, and an enduring stability with promises of peace. "The most important thing that comes out of leader-level meetings is that when the two leaders meet, they're able to build trust, and when they build trust, then everything else becomes easier," said Sean Stein, president of the U.S.-China Business Council. "So for us, that's the most important thing we're looking for when President Xi travels to Washington to meet President Trump," he added. WIN-WIN COOPERATION As China and the United States share broad common interests and vast potential for cooperation, Xi has emphasized the need to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, strengthen dialogue and consultation, and turn shared interests into concrete outcomes. China-U.S. economic ties are mutually beneficial and win-win in nature, Xi said in his meeting with Trump in May. During his state visit to China, Trump was accompanied by top U.S. executives, including Apple's Tim Cook, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Tesla's Elon Musk, whom he called outstanding representatives from the U.S. business community. "China will only open its door wider," Xi said during the meeting with Trump. American companies are deeply involved in China's reform and opening up, and the U.S. side is welcome to enhance mutually beneficial cooperation, he added. "As the world's two largest, most dynamic and most technologically advanced economies, it's just impossible for the U.S. and Chinese economies to function as well without a strong and viable relationship with the other, so it's absolutely essential," said Stein. Despite frictions and challenges, China-U.S. trade has demonstrated strong resilience. In the second quarter of this year, bilateral trade in goods grew 13.7 percent year on year. As of July this year, U.S. companies had established more than 84,000 enterprises in China. "What has happened demonstrates yet again that the description of China-U.S. cooperation benefiting both sides and confrontation hurting both sides reflects a common sense that has been repeatedly proven by experience, and the vision of China and the United States helping each other succeed and prosper together is a tangible prospect within reach," Xi said in a phone conversation with Trump in 2025. This year marks the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for economic and social development, and the 250th founding anniversary of the United States. As both countries enter pivotal stages of their respective development, new opportunities for cooperation are emerging. In July, a delegation of Chinese business leaders traveled to Salt Lake City, Chicago and Washington, D.C., where they met with representatives of more than 120 U.S. companies and organizations. Their discussions underscored that the appetite for cooperation remains strong. Across the U.S. business community, there is growing recognition of the vast potential for Chinese and U.S. companies to work together in cutting-edge fields, from green energy and the digital economy to artificial intelligence and biomedicine. Kate Sullivan, executive director of the Greater Columbus Chinese Chamber of Commerce, pointed to Illuminate USA, a joint-venture solar panel manufacturer in Columbus, Ohio, as a success story of China-U.S. cooperation. "It is the epitome of advanced manufacturing in the state of Ohio, drawing on multiple strengths of Chinese manufacturing and supply chains," she said. "It makes sense for the United States and China to be in business together. It's not an emotional decision there. It's business. Supply and demand." Looking ahead, business representatives also voiced expectations for a more stable environment for bilateral cooperation. "We hope the two heads of state will maintain strategic communication, bringing greater stability, stronger confidence and a longer-term outlook to markets and businesses in both countries," said Wang Qi, chairman of the U.S.-China Green Energy Council. PEOPLE-TO-PEOPLE EXCHANGES Xi has consistently emphasized that the foundation and future of China-U.S. relations ultimately lie in the connections between the two peoples. "Though geographically far apart, our peoples boast a long history of friendly exchanges," Xi said in a speech at a welcoming dinner hosted by local governments and friendly organizations in Seattle in 2015. Over the years, Xi has maintained close personal ties with people from all walks of life in the United States. In 2015, Xi visited Lincoln High School in the U.S. port city of Tacoma. Without a tie, he presented gifts to the students, including books on China, a ping-pong table, and his personal invitation for the students to visit China. In 2023, before the Welcome Dinner by Friendly Organizations in San Francisco, Xi met with veterans of the Flying Tigers and descendants of late General Joseph Stilwell, whose stories have become an important part of the history of China-U.S. friendship. In 2024, in his reply to a letter from Lamont Repollet, president of Kean University in the United States, Xi encouraged universities in China and the United States to strengthen exchanges and cooperation and contribute to China-U.S. friendship. During this year's Spring Festival, Xi replied to friends in the U.S. state of Iowa and sent them a Chinese New Year card with festive greetings, continuing their warm exchange of New Year wishes for the third consecutive year. In 2023, during his visit to San Francisco, Xi announced that China was ready to invite 50,000 young Americans to China on exchange and study programs in the next five years. "We hope that our two peoples will make more visits, contacts and exchanges and write new stories of friendship in the new era," he said. The invitation was warmly received by young people in the United States. In just over two and a half years, more than 50,000 young Americans from all 50 states have traveled to China. Their trips have taken them to different parts of the country. They have toured smart factories, visited rural communities and experienced everyday life in places far from home. For many, the journeys have also led to new friendships with Chinese peers. "I am particularly grateful to President Xi for his initiative of 50,000 in five years. I think that is possibly one of the most consequential initiatives in the last 20 years," said Luca Berrone, a four-decade-long friend of Xi in Iowa. "I believe that people-to-people exchanges, particularly between China and the United States, are fundamental in continuing to strengthen the relationship, to improve understanding and acceptance," he said. (Video reporters: Mu Xuyao, Meng Jing, Xu Yang, Liu Chunhui, Yang Zhigang, Zhao Xu, Hu Yousong and You Zhixin; Video editors: Mu Xuyao, Liu Xiaorui, Zhao Tianlin, Wang Houyuan, Shi Peng and Shang Yang)■

item.title: Asian Games | Day 3: Chinese marksman Sheng takes third gold, China lifts title in women's volleyball
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
by sportswriter Li Jia NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese shooter Sheng Lihao claimed his third gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, setting two world records with his teammate, while the Chinese women's volleyball team lifted the title with a commanding 3-0 victory over Japan. The triumph marked China's 10th women's volleyball gold medal at the Asian Games and a rematch of the Hangzhou Games final between the two sides. Earlier in the day, Sheng, a two-time Olympic champion, and teammate Wang Zifei won the 10m air rifle mixed team title, setting world records in both qualification and the final. The 19-year-old Sheng has now won three golds in the games, having notched the men's 10m air rifle individual and team titles already. "I didn't expect to shoot that well. The score was much higher than what I usually get in training, so I think I was a little lucky," Sheng said. China continued to dominate in the pool. Peng Xuwei defended her women's 200m backstroke title in 2:05.77, breaking the previous Asian record set in 2010. China's Zhang Zhanshuo, 19, won the men's 1,500m freestyle in 14:42.42 for his second title of the Games. He had anchored China's men's 4x200m freestyle relay victory on Monday. Japan's Tabuchi Kaito and Imafuku Kazushi took silver and bronze respectively. Li Bingjie retained her women's 400m freestyle title, while China won the men's 4x100m medley relay. Xu Jiayu, Dong Zhihao, Xu Fang and Pan Zhanle clocked 3:27.89 for the title. With the relay gold, Xu and Pan both had collected three gold medals. Siobhan Haughey from Hong Kong, China defended the women's 100m freestyle title in 52.45 seconds, with China's Yu Yiting and Cheng Yujie taking silver and bronze. Japan's Yumeiki Kojima won the men's 400m individual medley in 4:07.02, ahead of teammate Tomoyuki Matsushita, while China's Wang Shun took bronze. In gymnastics, Japan ended China's run of 13 consecutive Asian Games titles in the women's all-around. Aiko Sugihara claimed the gold medal with 55.599, while China's Ke Qinqin took silver, finishing 0.4 points behind. "This is my first Asian Games. I hope to work hard and have the chance to compete at the Asian Games again in the future, and stand on the higher step of the podium in this event," said Ke. China's Guo Li collected women's cycling road race gold after completing the 90.4-kilometer race in two hours, 50 minutes and five seconds, edging Afghanistan's Fariba Hashimi in a sprint finish. Hashimi took silver while Leung Wing Yee of Hong Kong, China finished third. China swept Thailand 3-0 in the women's team quarterfinals of badminton, while the men's team edged South Korea 3-2 to advance to the semifinals. China also secured places in both table tennis team semifinals, with the men's team beating Thailand 3-1 and the women's team easing past Uzbekistan 3-0. After three days of competition, China led the medal table with 32 gold, 13 silver and eight bronze medals. Japan was second with 11 gold, 16 silver and 19 bronze medals, followed by South Korea with six gold, four silver and 17 bronze medals. ■

item.title: China holds exhibition to mark 90th anniversary of Long March victory
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, addresses the opening ceremony of a themed exhibition commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 22, 2026. The exhibition opened Tuesday at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution in Beijing. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- A themed exhibition commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March opened Tuesday at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution in Beijing. In his address at the opening ceremony, Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, said the victory stunned the world and continues to shine in the annals of history. Cai stressed that the victory of the Long March marked a great turning point for the CPC and the Chinese revolution, and stands as a towering monument in the historic process of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The Long March was an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936, during which the CPC-led Red Army broke through encirclement by Kuomintang forces. Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. The maneuver helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Cai said the spirit forged through the sacrifices of Chinese Communists and Red Army soldiers continues to inspire the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and advance from victory to victory. The exhibition provides an important platform for education on ideals and convictions, patriotism and revolutionary traditions, he said, calling for carrying forward the Long March spirit on the new journey. The exhibition comprises seven main sections, including the Zunyi Meeting, major military operations and the enduring legacy of the Long March. English captions accompany each exhibit. The exhibition takes up approximately 3,300 square meters on the western side of the museum's third floor, with a display route stretching more than 760 meters. It features 875 cultural relics or sets of relics, a substantial increase from previous exhibitions in 2006 and 2016. The museum also said it is displaying 186 historical documents, 357 photographs and charts, 73 artworks and 16 videos. According to the museum, more than 300 relics and documents are being exhibited for the first time, accounting for approximately 28 percent of the total number of relics and documents on display. The exhibition also presents 60 stories from the Long March. It features 14 scenes depicting key episodes, including the Battle of the Xiangjiang River, the Zunyi Meeting and the Four Crossings of the Chishui River. About 600 people, including officials, military personnel and representatives from various walks of life, attended the opening ceremony. Cai and other leaders toured the exhibition with members of the public afterward. ■ Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, visits a themed exhibition commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 22, 2026. item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to 48th WorldSkills Competition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter on Tuesday to the 48th WorldSkills Competition. Xi noted that a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing rapidly, exerting a profound impact on global skills development. Closely aligned with the needs of industries, the WorldSkills Competition provides a useful platform for skilled professionals from various countries to hone their skills and learn from each other, Xi said. Xi stressed that China will take the opportunity of hosting this year's competition to encourage and guide more workers, especially young people, to pursue a path to success through skills. "China is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with all parties, promote the development of the WorldSkills movement, and better contribute to global economic growth and the improvement of people's well-being," Xi said. The 48th WorldSkills Competition opened in Shanghai the same day under the theme "Master Skills Change Your Future." Hosted by WorldSkills International and jointly organized by China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, the competition will also feature the WorldSkills Conference and WorldSkills Expo. ■

item.title: Xi extends greetings ahead of farmers' harvest festival
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has extended festive greetings and sincere regards on behalf of the CPC Central Committee to farmers and people working on agricultural and rural fronts ahead of the ninth Chinese farmers' harvest festival. Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, stressed the importance of solid efforts to advance all-around rural revitalization and ensure that farmers live happier and better lives. Xi noted that this year, China's summer grain output hit a new record and early rice output remained stable, while a bumper autumn harvest is within sight. Party committees and governments at all levels should work to ensure that policies aimed at strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching rural areas deliver greater outcomes and enhance the overall production capacity, quality and performance of agriculture, he said. Efforts should be made to expand channels for rural residents to increase incomes and build a beautiful and harmonious countryside for people to live and work in, based on local conditions, Xi said. The Chinese farmers' harvest festival is the first national festival created specifically for the country's farmers. This year's festival falls on Wednesday. Launched in 2018, the festival coincides with the Autumnal Equinox each year, which is one of the 24 solar terms of the Chinese lunisolar calendar and usually falls between Sept. 22 and 24 during the country's agricultural harvest season. ■
